combination._provenance: Measured, not assumed. A real run of the combination probe (experiments/phase2-probe/mechanism_probe.py, jobType=combination) over this exact member list reported: orderMatchesDeclared=true, executionCounts={module-aspp-v1:3, module-se-v1:3}, and 15 parameter tensors in the composition. The counts below are those numbers, split by owner. `combination-owned: 2` is the stack head (stack.head.weight/bias) that fixtures/phase2-probe/stack_fixture.py adds and that NO member owns; it is declared explicitly so a head that grows parameters fails the attribution check rather than passing unnoticed.
combination._sharedStateNote: Empty is a FACT, not an omission: each module reads only its own input and returns a new tensor; neither writes to a buffer the other reads. The combination.shared_state rule still runs and would fail if a module started writing shared state without declaring it.

_bindingScope: The binding above is the TWO-module composition declared by configs/phase2/execution-config.json rows.modules (module-aspp-v1 + module-se-v1). It is still a CHAIN PROOF, not a research result under the default source bundle, whose proposal is kind=manual pointing at PHASE2-RPD.md. Phase 3 switches to a P6 research proposal by selecting the source pack's `researchBundle` (same pinned sources, kind:research candidate-P002), which is why `phase2-module-attention-gate-v1` is in allowedPaths and in the registry's pinned table; the Phase 3 chain binds it explicitly in its own request. The mechanism checks above are mechanism-class driven, so a parameterized_feature module is checked by the parameterized.* set regardless of which proposal selected it.
